title: Finite-Tor direct image and scalar projection over an arbitrary field
statement: Let $k$ have characteristic $p>0$ and let $\ell\ne p$ be prime. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, let $R=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $t$, and put $A=R/t^nR$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $h:U\to V$ be a $k$-morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Work in ordinary constant-ring module derived categories on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $D^b_{ctf}$ for bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, meaning that tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. There is $c_h\geq0$ such that $R^qh_*M=0$ for every $A$-module sheaf $M$ and $q>c_h$. If $K\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, $a\leq b$, then $Rh_*K$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(V,A)$ with Tor amplitude $[a,b+c_h]$. For every unital finite commutative $A$-algebra $B$, scalar extension $T_W=-\otimes_A^LB_W$ takes $D^b_{ctf}(W,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(W,B)$ for $W=U,V$, preserving the Tor interval. The canonical $B$-linear comparison $T_VRh_{*,A}K\to Rh_{*,B}T_UK$, defined as the transpose of the scalar-extended inverse-image/direct-image counit, is an isomorphism. Upon exact restriction of scalars it is the finite-constant projection map followed by the canonical direct-image restriction comparison [def-kun-projection-formula-map, lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. No flatness of $B/A$ or absolute cohomological-dimension bound for $k$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use finite_coefficientExtensionRing for finiteness of A and the finite-ring Noetherian instance. The chosen DVR maximal ideal contains ell because its spectral absolute value is less than one; its chosen uniformizer generates that ideal. Ideal.pow_mem_pow and the quotient kernel give ell^n=0 in A. Primality of p=char(k) and ell != p imply ell, hence ell^n, is a unit in k and in the global sections of Spec(k). Every finite A-algebra B, viewed as an A-module, is finitely presented over the finite Noetherian ring A.

proof.text: Choose a natural number d bounding the topological Krull dimension of U, using finite type over k. Apply the already-proved source-library isZero_rightDerived_lowerStar_of_two_mul_lt to the finite, hence additively torsion, ring A. It gives vanishing of all higher direct images above c=2*d. The homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso identifies these with H^q(Rh_*(M[0])), giving the required uniform bound without an absolute bound on k.

proof.text: By [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility], $F=Rh_*K$ is bounded constructible: $A$ is finite killed by the invertible integer $\ell^n$, and $h$ is a morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes; separatedness is unnecessary. Apply [lem-pur-etale-residue-direct-image-tor-window] with this $F$, Step 1's coefficients and Step 2's bound. Its interval is exactly $[a,b+c_h]$, so $F\in D^b_{ctf}(V,A)$.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.17, finite-constant projection; residue test expanded in the cited DAG node

proof.text: Finite-type schemes U and V over the field k are Noetherian. A bounded constructible J has some lower and upper cohomology bounds. Package it as an object of DerivedCategory.Bounded and apply exists_etaleScalarFlatModel for the finite ring map A->B. Its final clauses give a bounded B-complex isomorphic to the actual scalar extension, constructible cohomology, and unchanged Tor interval [r,s]. Transport the boundedness along the isomorphism and combine with constructibility. In particular this applies to K and Rh_*K, giving the bounded-below witnesses for the normalized mate theorem.

source.place: Paragraph (2): bounded flat constructible model in degrees [a,b] and its termwise scalar extension, stated on the ordinary etale site by the cited flat-model node

proof.text: Apply the proved private finiteConstantProjectionComponent_isIso from the finite-constant projection theorem to K and the finitely presented A-module underlying B. The canonical constant-sheaf/restriction isomorphism, mapped into degree zero, identifies its coefficient object with scalarCoefficient phi V; naturality transports invertibility to this projection component. Apply the existing proved scalarMate_isIso_of_projection helper: using lower bounds for K and its actual scalar extension, it combines the normalized mate equation, invertibility of the bounded-below direct-image restriction comparison and reflection of isomorphisms by exact restriction. Finally scalarMate_restrict_eq_projection with the bounded-below witnesses for K and its two scalar extensions gives exactly the required equality, with the specified scalar/tensor and coefficient-pullback identifications.
